data.narrative:
Remora, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Eric Harding, Paul Gross, and Christina Reynolds, has raised $175M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparative universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (LNZA) operating in the same sector and stage band, including peers such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised ($175M) as a proxy base and applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $332M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yielded a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals). The peer-median approach reflects the full distribution of valuations in this segment and provides an anchor closer to later-stage multiples.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $283M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $666M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty: performance variance among climate-tech businesses remains pronounced, and publicly traded comparables in this space are limited. Stage-progression methods anchor conservatively; peer multiples capture market pricing but depend heavily on whether Remora's technology and market position align with the highest-valued cohort. Key sensitivities include deployment traction, technology differentiation relative to the peer set, and market-rate capital availability in climate tech.
